resources.string: This is not a medical diagnosis. It compares how well you hear different pitches in each ear, to tune your music and to tell you when a hearing test with an audiologist is a good idea.

Find a quiet place, put your headphones on the right way round and turn off noise cancelling. It takes about five minutes. You will hear short beeps in one ear at a time: tap “I hear it” as soon as you hear one, even a faint one.
Play the reference tone and set your volume so it sounds clear and comfortable, never loud. Do not change the volume during the check: the tones will be this loud or quieter.
Quietest tone you heard, in dB below your reference volume. Lower is better; only differences between ears and pitches mean something.
Your ears responded evenly across the pitches tested. If you notice ringing, muffled hearing or pain, see an audiologist anyway.
One ear heard noticeably less well than the other at several pitches. Please see an audiologist for a proper hearing test.
Some pitches were much harder to hear than others. Please see an audiologist for a proper hearing test.
WaveHeaven can keep this result as an equaliser curve in a new listening profile, lifting the pitches you hear less well a little.
Saved as the “My hearing” profile and selected.
